name: Beechcraft King Air 200/250/350 / C-12 Huron
summary: The T-tail Super King Air family, the US military's most widespread light twin as the C-12/UC-12 Huron, RC-12 Guardrail, MC-12 and the Navy's T-54A trainer.

wings: Low, straight wing; winglets on the 350/360 and some 250/260s
engines: Two PT6A turboprops in long nacelles with exhaust stacks pointing outboard
fuselage: Longer cabin than the 90-series with more rounded-square windows
RC-12/MC-12: many antennas, wing-mounted pods or belly radomes
tail: Small ventral strakes under the tail on the 350

tellTales: T-tail on a pressurized twin turboprop with a mid-length cabin
Exhaust stacks pointing outward from long engine nacelles

confusedWith.howToTell: The 200/250/350 has a T-tail and a longer cabin; the 90-series has a low tailplane (except the F90) and a short cabin.
The King Air is shorter with fewer, larger windows; the 1900 is a long airliner with many small windows and small stabilons on the tail cone.
The King Air is a twin; the PC-12 is a single-engine turboprop, though both have T-tails.
